known_final_diagnosis: SARS-CoV2 induced LVO and atherosclerotic mediated LVO were high on the differential, including haemorrhagic stroke, seizures and meningitis. The most likely differential is SARS-CoV2-induced LVO due to SARS-CoV-2 hypercoagulable properties and non-tandem occlusions of the patient’s cerebral vasculature including the LICA and proximal RVA. The AIS progressed to a multilobar infarct manifesting as right-sided facial droop with upper and lower extremity flaccidity with associated hyperactive delirium.

clinician.final_diagnosis: SARS-CoV2 induced LVO and atherosclerotic mediated LVO causing acute ischemic stroke with multilobar infarct and hyperactive delirium
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man with multiple vascular risk factors presented with viral prodromal symptoms, pneumonia, acute kidney injury, and lymphopenia. On day 7, he developed new neurological deficits including right-sided facial droop and flaccid upper and lower extremities with altered speech. Non-contrast CT head showed no acute bleed, and aspirin, clopidogrel, and atorvastatin were started. CTA revealed multiple large vessel occlusions with complete occlusion of the left internal carotid artery and proximal right vertebral artery along with high-grade stenosis of the right internal carotid artery. EEG showed focal slowing in left parietal and posterior brain regions, indicating brain dysfunction. The patient’s respiratory status worsened requiring intubation and ICU transfer. Lower extremity Doppler ultrasound demonstrated progression of deep vein thrombosis. Although laboratory coagulation parameters and detailed neurological course including delirium progression and ruling out seizures or meningitis were not documented, available evidence supports a COVID-19 related hypercoagulable state causing multiple cerebral large vessel occlusions leading to acute ischemic stroke with clinical progression consistent with multilobar infarction and hyperactive delirium.
